newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan to enter talks with India with open mind.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan to enter talks with India with open mind.

text.p: Pakistan said on Wednesday it would approach talks with India in a "sincere and open frame of mind" to try to solve all issues, including the Kashmir dispute.
"There is no change on Pakistan's position on the Kashmir issue with the change of government," the official news agency APP quoted Foreign Office spokesman Khalid Saleem as saying.

"We will be going to India with a sincere and open frame of mind and hope India would respond in the same spirit," he said of talks between the secretaries of the Indian and Pakistan foreign ministries set for March 28-31 in New Delhi.
Saleem said Pakistan had always wanted "cooperative, tension-free and good neighbourly relations" with India.
"We feel this is a historic opportunity to make a beginning towards this end," he said.
He said Pakistan's new government led by Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif was committed to improving relations with India, but declined to disclose its negotiating strategy.
Saleem said Pakistan did not expect the Delhi talks to produce an immediate agreement. "I am neither optimistic nor pessimistic about the outcome of the talks," he declared.

The Delhi talks will revive a dialogue that foundered in January 1994 over the disputed territory of Kashmir, of which India controls two thirds and Pakistan the rest. Saleem said Sharif's letter to his Indian counterpart H.D. Deve Gowda had made clear Pakistan wanted some progress on the Kashmir issue as a prerequisite for talks on other issues.

Asked about statements by Indian leaders that Kashmir is an integral part of India, Saleem said: "We don't take such public statements at their face value... If you read intentions in public statements then you can never start negotiations."
He said the talks would cover all issues, including the military standoff at the high-altitude Siachen glacier.
